newsitem.title: FRANCE: French naval base workers exposed to radioactivity.
newsitem.headline: French naval base workers exposed to radioactivity.

text.p: Some 30 civilian workers assembling nuclear warheads for submarine missiles at a navy base in western France have been exposed to low levels of radioactivity, authorities said on Monday.
Navy authorities in charge of the submarine base at L'Ile Longue near the port of Brest said the workers had suffered irradiation "very slightly higher" than the allowed level of five millisieverts.
The Defence Ministry said the civilians were assembling new-generation TN-75 missile warheads whose radioactivity is higher than the previous TN-70 and TN-71 warheads.
Fresh security measures were being implemented in order to step up radioactivity controls, it said.
The ministry denied a newspaper report that the radioactivity could be due to a leak in the nuclear propulsion system of the submarine Le Triomphant.
"No fault has to this day been detected regarding Le Triomphant, either in its weapons system or in its nuclear machine room," a ministry statement said.
Navy authorities said that norms in civilian nuclear facilities allowed work to go on until radioactivity reached 50 millisieverts.

The new TN-75 warheads for France's missile-carrying nuclear submarines were validated in a controversial series of six nuclear tests in the South Pacific which ended last January. France has since pledged not to carry out any more nuclear tests.
